title: Pentatonic — The Global Scale
body: Pentatonic appears independently worldwide: China, Japan, Africa, Scotland, the Andes, blues. Anhemitonic (no semitones) is clash-proof — the piano's black keys are exactly it.

title: Blues & the African Diaspora
body: Blue notes flatten the 3rd, 5th, 7th 'between the keys'; the 12-bar form is the most famous progression on Earth. The blues scale parented jazz, rock, R&B and soul.

title: Tuning & Microtonality
body: Pure ratios don't close: 12 perfect fifths overshoot the octave. Just intonation is sweet but breaks in distant keys; equal temperament splits the octave into 12 equal semitones — every key usable, every interval slightly impure.

title: Rhythmic Traditions
body: West African bell timelines, Cuba's 3-2/2-3 clave, India's tala cycles, Balkan aksak 'limping' metres (7/8 = 2+2+3), and 3-against-4 polyrhythm. Western barlines are one culture among many.

title: Instruments of the World
body: Chordophones (sitar, koto, kora), aerophones (shakuhachi, didgeridoo), membranophones (tabla, djembe), idiophones (gongs, mbira). Every instrument encodes its culture's theory.

title: Andes: Siku & Pentatonic Wind
body: The siku comes in paired halves (ira/arca) — two players interlock one melody, hocketing. Quena sings solos; charango and bombo complete the blend.

title: Andes: Huayno & Nueva Canción
body: Huayno: 2/4 bouncing behind the beat; yaraví is its mournful sibling ('El Cóndor Pasa'). Nueva canción fused it with protest — Violeta Parra to Los Kjarkas.

title: Celtic: Modes & Dance Metres
body: Irish/Scottish melody is intensely modal over drones. Jig 6/8, reel 4/4, hornpipe swung, strathspey's Scotch snap. Eight-bar AABB tunes chain into sets; cuts and rolls ornament by ear.

title: Celtic: Sessions & the Fringe
body: The session — no scores, shared repertoire — is the engine. Sean-nós ornaments unaccompanied song. The fringe is wide: Wales, Breton fest-noz, Galician gaita, Cape Breton.

title: Flamenco: Compás & Palos
body: Soleá accents 3-6-8-10-12 of 12; bulerías flip to start on 12. Tonality is Phrygian driven by the Andalusian cadence Am–G–F–E.

title: Klezmer: Modes & the Bulgar
body: Freygish ('Jewish major') = flat 2 with major 3. The doina improvises free; the bulgar drives weddings in 2/4. The krekhts 'sob' makes the clarinet weep on cue.

title: Ethiopia: The Qenet Modes
body: Tizita (nostalgia), bati, ambassel, anchihoye — pentatonics that resist the piano. Azmari poets improvise; Mulatu's Ethio-jazz fuses qenet with funk.

title: Georgia: Polyphonic Table Songs
body: Three by-ear parts — bass drone, moving middle, soaring top — in open fourths and deliberate dissonances. Gurian krimanchuli yodels between registers.

title: Brazil: Samba & Bossa Nova
body: Samba: surdos on 2-and-4, tamborim teleco-teco on top. Bossa added João Gilberto's hushed guitar under Jobim's 7ths and 9ths.

title: Tuvan & Mongolia: Khoomei
body: Throat singing amplifies the overtone series: a low fundamental drones while the vocal tract boosts one partial at a time — a whistling melody above.

title: Bulgaria: Choir & Odd Metres
body: Open-throated choirs built on sharp-2nd clashes. Metres are additive: 7/8 (2+2+3), 11/8 kopanitsa (2+2+2+3+2) — danced by body, not numbers.

title: Cuba: The Son
body: The tres guitar's guajeo riff rides the son clave while bongó, bass and trumpet answer in call-and-response montunos. 'Chan Chan' is the classic texture.

title: Portugal: Fado
body: Lisbon's urban lament: one voice against the bell-like 12-string Portuguese guitar, wrapped in saudade — longing for the absent.

title: Argentina: Tango
body: Bandoneón, violin, piano and bass weave melancholy for dancers in close embrace. Piazzolla dragged it into 'nuevo'; the Golden Age still rules the milongas.

title: Hawai'i: Slack Key & Steel
body: Kī hō'alu slackens strings into open tunings (Taro Patch = open G) so one thumb carries bass and rhythm. Hawai'i also invented the lap steel (c.1900).

title: Aboriginal Australia: Songlines
body: Songlines map country through song. The yidaki (didgeridoo) drones with circular breathing into animal voices; clapsticks keep time. Listen with respect.
